newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil sees steady first half profit.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil sees steady first half profit.

text.p: Soft-drink bottler Coca Cola Amatil Ltd said on Thursday that its net profit for the calendar 1997 first half should be in line with the year ago result.
Chairman Dean Wills told the annual general meeting that on this basis the company should achieve "an enhanced result" for the full year.
Wills said the company should post an increase in trading profit for the 1997 first half.
"In net profit terms this should translate into a result in line with the company's 1996 first half," he said.
The company reported a 1996 first half net profit of A$58.9 million and an operating profit of A$94.4 million.
In calendar 1996, it achieved a net profit of A$142.10 million from A$138.60 million in 1995. The company is about 36 percent-owned by The Coca-Cola Co.

C-C Amatil shares have come under intense pressure this year due to broker downgrades based on the Australian company's disappointing profit growth performance which was below internal and outside forecasts. Its shares were 57 cents higher at A$12.52 in late Thursday morning trade.
